headline: 5 arrested after 13-month-old child allegedly sold for Tk 2 lakh in Mymensingh
summary: The child was rescued from Dhaka's Dohar upazila after the mother filed a case under the human trafficking law.
details: Police have arrested five people, including the child's grandfather and grandmother, for allegedly selling a 13-month-old baby for Tk 2 lakh in Mymensingh's Ishwarganj upazila.
The rescued child was found in the Harichandi area of Dohar upazila, Dhaka, following a police investigation into a general diary (GD) filed by the mother, Rozina Begum.
According to the case, Rozina was beaten and sent back to her parents' home five months ago due to family disputes. Her son, Mozahid, remained with the grandfather.

Rozina later learned from locals that her husband and in-laws had sold the child on September 28 night. When she tried to inquire about her son, she was allegedly abused and driven out of her in-laws' house.
The arrested individuals include the grandfather Ujjwal Mia (50), grandmother Aisha Khatun (45), aunt Sharifa Khatun (35), and a couple from Dohar, Abed Molla (35) and Shikha (35).
The couple from Dohar claimed they took the child to raise him because they had no children of their own, though police stated the process was illegal.
The child is currently safe with the police and will be handed over to the mother through the court. Further investigations are ongoing to identify other involved parties.

The arrested individuals include the grandfather Ujjwal Mia (50), grandmother Aisha Khatun (45), aunt Sharifa Khatun (35), and a couple from Dohar, Abed Molla (35) and Shikha (35).

headline_marked: 852m gap: [[Bangladesh Satellite-1 narrowly avoids collision]] with debris
headline: 852m gap: Bangladesh Satellite-1 narrowly avoids collision with debris
summary: Engineers at the Gazipur ground station successfully maneuvered the satellite to avoid an incoming piece of defunct Indian satellite debris.
details: On August 9, NASA informed the Bangladesh Satellite Company Limited (BSCL) that debris from a defunct Indian satellite was rapidly approaching Bangladesh Satellite-1 (BS-1).
The threat of a potential collision kept engineers at the Gazipur ground station in a state of high alert and anxiety for four days.
According to BSCL Managing Director Muhammad Imadur Rahman, engineers managed to slightly shift the position of BS-1 on August 13 despite limited options.
The debris eventually passed the satellite at a distance of 852 meters, avoiding a catastrophic impact.
This successful maneuver is being hailed as a significant achievement for the country's satellite engineers.
caption:
A piece of space debris was hurtling toward Bangladesh Satellite-1. Engineers had just enough room to move it out of the way.

On August 9, NASA informed the Bangladesh Satellite Company Limited (BSCL) that debris from a defunct Indian satellite was rapidly approaching Bangladesh Satellite-1 (BS-1).

The threat of a potential collision kept engineers at the Gazipur ground station in a state of high alert and anxiety for four days.

According to BSCL Managing Director Muhammad Imadur Rahman, engineers managed to slightly shift the position of BS-1 on August 13 despite limited options.

The debris eventually passed the satellite at a distance of 852 meters, avoiding a catastrophic impact.

This successful maneuver is being hailed as a significant achievement for the country's satellite engineers.
